title: Finite translates of a rational cone under a finite-kernel quotient
statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group, let $L$ be a free abelian group of finite rank (an abelian group with a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module], for the canonical action by integer multiples), and let $\pi:G\to L$ be a surjective group homomorphism with finite kernel $K=\{g\in G:\pi(g)=0\}$. Choose a finite list $p_1,\ldots,p_r\in G$, allowing $r=0$; it is not required to generate $G$ as a group. Set
$$P=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^r n_i p_i:n_i\in\mathbf N\right\},\qquad C=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^r q_i\pi(p_i):q_i\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\right\}\subseteq L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q,$$
and identify $L$ with its image under $\ell\mapsto\ell\otimes1$. Define $Q=\{g\in G:\pi(g)\in C\}$. There exists a finite subset $F\subseteq Q$ such that
$$Q=\bigcup_{f\in F}(f+P),\qquad f+P=\{f+p:p\in P\}.$$
No sharpness of $P$, pointedness of $C$, or torsion-freeness of $G$ is assumed.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.2.9 proof, printed p. 104 (finite toric saturation input); agent expansion: Gordan finite translates in the lattice followed by the finite-kernel lifting argument of the returned parent proof, Step 1.

proof.text: Put $v_i=\pi(p_i)$ and $P_L=\{\sum_i n_i v_i:n_i\in\mathbf N\}$. Since $L$ has a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis and the list $v_i$ is finite, [lem-trf-gordan-rational-cone-finite] applies, including $r=0$. It supplies a finite $E\subseteq C\cap L$ with $C\cap L=\bigcup_{e\in E}(e+P_L)$. The cone and lattice embedding are precisely those of the item. Moreover $P_L=\pi(P)$: applying $\pi$ to $\sum_i n_i p_i$ gives $\sum_i n_i v_i$, and every expression on the latter side has the former lift.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 proof, printed p.104, finite toric saturation assertion; agent expansion by the existing lattice finite-translate lemma and explicit finite-fibre lifting.

proof.text: Define $F=\pi^{-1}(E)\subseteq G$. For each $e\in E$, surjectivity gives $a_e\in G$ with $\pi(a_e)=e$. Its fibre is exactly $a_e+K$: for $g$ in that fibre, $\pi(g-a_e)=e-e=0$, whereas for $k\in K$, $\pi(a_e+k)=e$. Thus $F=\bigcup_{e\in E}(a_e+K)$ is a finite union of images of the finite set $K$, hence finite. Since $E\subseteq C$, its full inverse image $F$ is contained in $Q$. No choice of an additive splitting of $\pi$ is involved.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 proof, printed p.104, finite toric saturation assertion; agent expansion by the existing lattice finite-translate lemma and explicit finite-fibre lifting.

proof.text: For $g\in Q$, Step 1 writes $\pi(g)=e+\sum_i n_i v_i$ with $e\in E$ and $n_i\in\mathbf N$. Put $p=\sum_i n_i p_i\in P$ and $f=g-p$. Then $\pi(f)=e$, so $f\in F$ and $g=f+p$. Hence $Q\subseteq\bigcup_{f\in F}(f+P)$. Conversely, if $f\in F$ and $p\in P$, then $\pi(f)\in E\subseteq C$ and $\pi(p)\in P_L\subseteq C$. Adding their nonnegative rational coefficient expressions shows $\pi(f+p)\in C$, so $f+p\in Q$. This proves the asserted equality. The proof uses neither generation of $G$ by the $p_i$, nor pointedness, nor absence of torsion in $G$.

The statement is unchanged and there are no new nodes. Step 1 cites the same-unit, already-split lem-trf-gordan-rational-cone-finite. Its statement (finite Z-basis, r=0 allowed, same cone C in L⊗Q and same natural-combination monoid) gives a finite E with C∩L=⋃(e+P_L), and P_L=π(P) follows in one line. Step 2 is elementary: F=π⁻¹(E) is a finite union of the fibres a_e+K, using surjectivity and the finite kernel, and F⊆Q. Step 3 is elementary: both inclusions are correct and use only additivity of C. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses, and there is no cycle. I tested r=0 (F=K), Z⊕Z/2 with generator (2,0) (full fibres are needed), a cone that is a whole line, and a generator that does not span L; the statement holds in each. The parent fine-monoid-finite-saturation uses exactly this form, with π:G→G/T and Q=P^sat. Source: ILO VIII 3.2.9, printed p.104, states only finiteness of S[F^sat]→S[F], so proof_origin=agent is honest. No SGA is cited. My DAG grep found no duplicate; lem-sfb-finite-kernel-group-fibres is about group schemes and is unrelated. No repair note applies and no tool_uses are needed.
